facts.fact: Central Bank of Liberia Governor Henry Saamoi said on 2026-11-18 that the Central Bank runs the Inclusive Instant Payment System, which connects the country's two mobile money operators and processes government payments.

LBR.note: Nothing on civil servant digital skills training.
Mentions affordability of charges only; no rules or complaints body stated.

facts.fact: The Central Bank governor said civil servants now receive salary payments in real time through the IPS, initiated by the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning and processed through the Central Bank.

LBR.note: Extension to chiefs and nurses is only planned.
States a 52% financial inclusion rate with no survey or account-ownership basis.

facts.fact: The Central Bank governor said Liberia's IPS is in use for person-to-person transfers and has processed millions of transactions.
The IPS connected Liberia's two mobile money operators so their platforms support transfers across previously separate systems, said the Central Bank governor.

LBR.note: The National Electronic Payment Switch is only targeted for Q1 2027.
Person-to-government tax payments are only being worked toward; no pilot or contract stated.
